event.active_recruitment_existing_cast_0: You remove your name from the ledger and leave. {{npc_ari}} stays alone with the patient and the inspectors.
Erase only your trace
You occupy the inspectors while {{npc_ari}} evacuates the patient. She meets you at the exit point.
Hold the door while she leaves
You make room for the patient and {{npc_ari}}. She closes the false file and leaves with you.
Take Ari and the patient
{{npc_ari}} is hiding an injured patient under a false name when inspectors enter the clinic. She recognizes you from your last triage and puts the back-door key in front of you.
The Patient Without a Real Name
You ask her to stay with the port. {{npc_ari}} agrees, though the exhaustion shows.
Ask Ari to stay
You stabilize the last patients and close the ward. {{npc_ari}} finally leaves the ledger and comes with you.
Close the shift together
You pay for overnight relief. {{npc_ari}} hands over the files and agrees to leave with you.
Fund the medical handover
After the overflowing clinic, {{npc_ari}} is still holding an East Blue quarantine ward. The promised relief never arrives; the last healthy ship leaves before dawn.
The Relief That Never Comes
The bollard gives way. The ferry leaves without you, and your friend takes the hit beside you.
You hold the ferry in front of the whole quay. Your friend joins you without asking twice.
The ferry leaves. Your old rule is not enough to stop a running line.
You stop the line together. This time, your old rule becomes a place in your crew.
Hold the ferry together
You repeat the rule you invented as children. Your friend smiles, grabs a bag, and comes with you.
Honor your old rule
You let the ferry go. Your friend understands that your roads are not joining yet.
Let the ferry go
{{npc_childhood_friend}} is holding the last line of an overloaded ferry alone. The skipper wants to cast off without them; your old game rule comes back word for word.
The Last Ferry
Your fake order makes them laugh; they call reinforcements and split your group.
The whole quay repeats your fake order. Your friend passes with you while the guards correct their own ledgers.
They hesitate, then demand a seal you do not have.
They open the passage just enough. Your friend follows before they understand.
Bluff the quay men
The blade slips; the men seal the quay and your friend is trapped behind them.
You cut cleanly and free the next boat too. Your friend boards while the quay erupts in confusion.
The line holds long enough for the men to retake the passage.
The line drops. Your friend jumps aboard as a watch boat turns toward you.
Cut the mooring in front of them
You leave under your flag. Your friend stays on the quay, furious that the symbol mattered more than your history.
Let the flag decide
Port men pin {{npc_childhood_friend}} against stacked crates and demand they denounce you as a pirate. Your friend refuses, then looks toward your ship.
The Quay Under Your Flag
You break line of sight under the pilings and emerge behind the warehouses.
Slip under the pier
You escape the watch boat, but your reunion already starts with a separation.
Split and regroup
Your nerve costs them a few seconds; enough to leave the basin.
Wave like you belong
A watch boat is already cutting across the basin. {{npc_childhood_friend}} points at the pilings, then your ship: your first crew decision comes before you even leave port.
The Watch Boat Turns
The list turns to ash. Your friend closes the hideout and leaves with you before the patrol arrives.
Burn the list and leave
You memorize the useful contacts, then destroy the paper. Your friend joins your crew with the network intact.
Save the names before leaving
You refuse to mix your friend into your cell. They nod, but the old rule now sounds like an excuse.
Keep your distance
Three knocks repeat the rhythm of your childhood game. {{npc_childhood_friend}} opens a compromised hideout: a contact list is still on the table and a patrol is approaching.
Three Knocks at the Door
You sign the report. {{npc_owen}} does not argue; he takes back the tools without looking at you.
Accept the yard report
You point to the wrong part; the yard bills the teardown to {{npc_owen}} and you.
You also find the old repair number. The yard backs down; {{npc_owen}} leaves with you.
The hull stays ambiguous enough for the foreman to keep the accusation alive.
You find a crack painted over long before his work. {{npc_owen}} returns the yard tools and accepts your berth.
Find the old crack
Nobody will risk their wages for you. The foreman isolates {{npc_owen}} further.
The whole crew refuses to sign the false report. {{npc_owen}} follows you before the foreman finds another scapegoat.
A few workers doubt the story, but not enough to challenge the ledger.
Two workers speak up. {{npc_owen}} puts down the yard hammer and chooses to work with you.
Turn the yard crew around
After the quay notice, {{npc_owen}} stops you beside an opened hull. The foreman wants him to sign for an old break as if his repair caused it.
The Crack They Blame on Him
You let the yard wall up the passage. {{npc_owen}} stays to see who comes looking for it.
Leave the keel to the yard
The wall gives way. {{npc_owen}} recognizes an old smuggling passage and decides to leave with you.
Open the false wall
You close it with a removable panel. {{npc_owen}} keeps the layout in mind and joins your group.
Seal it your way
{{npc_owen}} finds a false wall inside a keel under repair. Old marks show it carried fugitives; the yard wants it sealed before inspection.
The Wall Inside the Keel
The yard falls silent before the patrol reaches the slipway.
Drop the hammer
Your calm sells the repair as routine work and the patrol moves on.
Keep working like nothing is wrong
You step outside to talk while {{npc_owen}} clears the last marks from the wall.
Meet them outside
One last hammer blow carries too far. A patrol turns toward the yard while {{npc_owen}} is still closing the false wall fasteners.
One Hammer Blow Too Many
You push too fast; a load drops and the contract disappears with the foreman’s trust.
You crush the quota without an accident. Even the quay remembers you are better together.
You match the quota, not enough to make him change his books.
Your old contest becomes perfect rhythm. Your rival then refuses to work without you.
Beat the quota together
You take the advance and the only place. Your rival lets you win that score without congratulations.
Take the single place
The foreman makes you choose publicly. Your rival leaves the quay before you answer.
The foreman pays an advance for two. Your rival pockets their share and chooses to continue with you.
The contract remains for one person. Neither of you yields quickly enough.
You turn his numbers against him. Your rival signs beside you, then turns the contract into a shared departure.
Negotiate two places
A foreman recognizes your efficiency but will pay only one person. {{npc_childhood_rival}} places two tokens on his ledger, like when every chore became a score.
One Place for Two
You read the leader wrong: he truly orders the strike and locks down the quay.
You name every crack in his bluff. His own men lower their weapons and your rival follows you.
He hesitates but releases no one.
You notice his crew already rejects the forced recruitment. The bluff breaks; your rival comes with you.
Call their captain’s bluff
You refuse to turn this into another score. Your rival will get free another way, but not with you.
Refuse this contest
The leader drives you into the crates and keeps your rival under his blade.
You turn their own gangway against them. Your rival laughs and boards with you.
You hold the gangway, but not enough to clear it.
You take the gangway from the gang. Your rival counts the point, then chooses your side.
Win the gangway
A small pirate gang forces {{npc_childhood_rival}} toward its gangway while calling it “recruitment.” Your rival sees you, smiles without humor, and asks which of you will win this quay.
The Last Quay Score
You return the paper to the checkpoint. Your rival memorizes that score and vanishes through another exit.
Hand the manifest back
You mark the wrong crate. The patrol spots the trick and closes the checkpoint.
You also spot the copied signature. Your rival joins your group with enough proof to turn the checkpoint around.
The manifest stays ambiguous; your old competition is not enough to beat the ledger.
You find the doubled line. Your rival joins your group while one final stamp is still missing.
Find the false line
The guard recognizes the diversion and calls a superior.
The guard orders a second inspection elsewhere himself. Your rival crosses with you, hiding a smile.
He argues, but keeps the manifest and the passage.
The guard checks the wrong ledger. Your rival passes with you before he returns.
Make the guard doubt
{{npc_childhood_rival}} slips a manifest under your arm: two inks prove a prisoner shipment was added after inspection. A patrol is coming back toward the ledger.
The Two-Ink Manifest
Your false stamp closes the file cleanly before the guard returns.
Copy the last stamp
You leave the anomaly visible enough to trigger questions behind you.
Leave the proof visible
The proof disappears from the official ledger and stays in your hands.
Tear out the page
The passage is nearly clear, but {{npc_childhood_rival}} points to one empty box. Without the final stamp, the manifest will show exactly where your group forced the checkpoint.
The Last Stamp
You serve the last line before dismantling the stove. {{npc_rohan}} takes a bag and joins your group.
Finish the last pot
You move the pots before the seizure. {{npc_rohan}} decides this kitchen will travel with you now.
Move the whole kitchen
You protect your network and abandon the kitchen. {{npc_rohan}} stays to feed those still waiting.
Save only your contact
{{npc_rohan}} is serving a line of dockworkers when agents arrive to seize the relief kitchen. He recognizes your group and asks whether to save the meal, the gear, or the people.
The Seized Cooking Pot
You put the missing money on the counter. {{npc_rohan}} returns the apron and comes with you.
Cover the shortfall and leave
You refuse to enter his work dispute. {{npc_rohan}} returns to the stove, disappointed but not surprised.
Leave him to settle the contract
The boss turns the ledger against you and even charges for broken plates.
You also find the illegal deductions from the others. {{npc_rohan}} gets the missing pay and follows you out of the kitchen.
The books stay dirty enough for the boss to stall.
You find the erased hours. {{npc_rohan}} gets the missing pay and chooses to leave this kitchen with you.
Prove the missing wages
After your Baratie meeting, {{npc_rohan}} finds you in another East Blue kitchen. The owner has just erased three days of wages and blocks the door with his ledger.
The Unpaid Service
You leave through the delivery window with his bag and nothing else.
Leave through the window
The other workers stand beside you. The boss unlocks the door.
Make the boss open up
{{npc_rohan}} takes back the greasy recipe book and leaves everything else to the boss.
Take only his recipe book
The dispute is settled, but the boss has locked the exit and keeps {{npc_rohan}}’s notebook behind the counter. The other workers stop to watch.
The Kitchen Door
